Good morning, everyone. We've got the twelve-bed teaching garden proposal on the agenda for today's project huddle. As you all know, the concept has already been approved, and we're now at the stage where we need to confirm the site, purchasing, and student-safety requirements before I can sign off on the final campus project plan. The current draft calls for in-ground beds, a volunteer workday on October 18, approximately $3,000 from general funds, and standard latex gardening gloves.

Before I can approve this, I need to hear from each of you on your respective areas. Science teacher, please walk us through your instructional needs for the site. Facilities coordinator, let's talk about the location beside the science wing and any site considerations. Business manager, please confirm the purchasing and budget requirements. And school nurse, I'd like you to review the safety plan, particularly the choice of gloves and any student-safety considerations. Who would like to start?

transcript.text: Dr. Morgan, before we go further, I need to share something important. I just received the soil test results yesterday from the proposed garden site, and they measured lead at 180 parts per million. Our district garden standard requires removing the top six inches of soil and using raised beds at that reading. This means the current draft plan's in-ground beds won't meet our safety standard — we'll need to revise the plan to include raised beds and the soil remediation step. I haven't had a chance to enter the lab results into the project folder yet, but I wanted to flag this now since it directly affects the site plan, purchasing costs, and student safety.

Thank you all for these critical updates. Let me summarize what I'm hearing so I can make the right call here. Ms. Rivera, the soil test showing lead at 180 ppm means we must switch to raised beds and remove the top six inches of soil per our district standard — the in-ground beds in the draft won't work. Mr. Chen, the utility locate doesn't clear the site until October 28, so the October 18 workday needs to move, and we'll need the posted site permit before any excavation or assembly begins. Ms. Brooks, the $4,200 grant reimbursement is welcome news and should more than cover the revised costs, but every purchase must go through a proper purchase order before anything is ordered. Nurse Williams, the severe latex allergy means we switch to nitrile-only gloves and post an allergy-safety notice at the garden entrance.

Based on all of this, here's what I'm prepared to settle on: raised beds instead of in-ground, removal of the top six inches of soil, moving the volunteer workday to October 28, funding through the community-garden grant with proper purchase orders, nitrile-only gloves, and an allergy-safety notice at the entrance. The budget will need to be revised upward from $3,000 to account for raised beds, remediation, and nitrile gloves — Ms. Brooks, can you confirm what the revised total is likely to be? Before I sign off, I'll need each of you to get your documentation — soil test results, utility clearance, grant award confirmation, and the health review — into the project folder. Let me know if there are any objections or additional requirements I haven't captured.
